quellen.text: 🎃 New: the Halloween pack (until 1 Nov): cleanyour.tv/halloween Read in: 简体中文 · 正體中文 · Tiếng Việt · 日本語 · Italiano · Nederlands · Deutsch · Українська ## Start here | You have | Go to | |---|---| | **An Android TV or Google TV** | Quick start: a coding assistant does the work in about fifteen minutes. | | **A Samsung, LG, Roku, Vizio or Hisense VIDAA TV** | cleanyour.tv/not-android: CleanYourTV can't run there, but you can turn off the tracking with your remote. | | **Only an Android phone** | The community-built Clean Your TV app: no laptop, no coding agent. | | **Want to see it first** | What you get: screenshots of the new home screen. | **Official links:** cleanyour.tv and this repo. Other domains using the name, such as cleanyourtv.com, are not run by this project (#1004). How it works · Quick start · What you get · Supported TVs · Doing it by hand · The launcher · Restoring · Firmware updates · Questions · Contributing ## How it works Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Switch on USB debugging in the TV's developer options, allow your computer once, and the rest is standard Android tooling: | Step | What happens | |---|---| | **Back up** | The list of installed packages and settings. | | **Disable** | The manufacturer's telemetry, ad services, content rows and preloaded junk, with `pm disable-user`. Nothing is uninstalled, so a restore script can undo every step. | | **Install** | A small native launcher, made the default home screen. | **No root, no cable, nothing uninstalled, and a one-line restore if you change your mind.** The bloat differs by brand, so the prompt has your coding assistant discover it on your TV and ask before touching anything you might use. ## Quick start | You have | Do this | |---|---| | **A computer** | Use the prompt with a coding assistant: the three steps below. | | **A computer, no coding assistant** | Run the three steps yourself: the commands are in Doing it by hand. | | **Only an Android phone** | Use the community-built Clean Your TV app by @udhaykumarbala: connect, analyse, clean, in about five minutes. No laptop, no coding agent. | The three steps below are written for a coding assistant: the computer needs to be on the same Wi-Fi as the TV, with a shell on it, plus Python 3, a JDK from 17 through 22, and Android SDK platform 34 with build-tools 34 (the assistant builds the launcher there). Without an assistant, Doing it by hand is the same job, run by you, and it has the install commands. Any of these work: Claude Code (on 0G Private Computer or an Anthropic plan), Codex, Gemini CLI or Antigravity CLI. | Where | What to do | |---|---| | **1. On the TV** | Settings → Device Preferences → About → press OK on **Build** seven times → back → Developer options → **USB debugging** on. If you see a Network or ADB debugging toggle, turn that on too. Keep the TV on. | | **2. On your computer** | Clone the repo and open that folder in your assistant (`git clone https://github.com/Gathin23/cleanyourtv`), then paste `PROMPT.md` and fill in your TV model. | | **3. Follow along** | Accept "Allow USB debugging?" on the TV, then answer the checklist: which apps you use, the dock size and app order, whether to keep the voice assistant, Chromecast and updates. | Cloning matters: the assistant reuses this repo's `tools/disable.sh` and `launcher/build-and-install.sh` instead of writing its own, and that is where the backup, the Home guard and the restore record live. The assistant backs up, debloats, builds and installs the launcher, and checks each step with screenshots pulled from the TV. With this repo as context it takes about fifteen minutes. ## What you get A home screen that looks like an Apple TV and gets out of the way: | Part | What it looks like | |---|---| | **A pitch-black home** | A dock of your four favourite apps in a rounded band, where Apple TV puts it. | | **A top shelf** | Names the focused app in large type, with an ambient glow in a colour taken from its artwork. | | **The rest of your apps in a grid** | Slides up when you press Down. | | **One floating glass highlight** | Springs from tile to tile. The focused tile lifts and shows its name. | | **Three frosted buttons** | Inputs (HDMI ports under the names you gave them in the TV's settings, AV, Live TV), Wi-Fi or Ethernet with the network name, Settings. | | **A greeting, a thin clock and the date** | In Outfit, and a matching Clock screensaver. Set `show_stats` in config or a theme for one line

quellen.name: TV Detox README (MIT, 1,947 stars, checked 2026-10-31)
quellen.text: # TV Detox ### Make an old, slow Android TV fast again. Claude Code or Codex does the work. You just press OK on the remote. **As seen on** All press coverage → 🧹 Removes the junk Bloatware, ads and sponsored rows, gone. 📺 A calm home screen Your apps, your HDMI inputs and a clock. Nothing else. ↩️ Undo anytime Apps are turned off, never deleted. ## Watch it work **▶ Claude Made My Old Android TV Feel Brand New** · the full setup on a real TV, in 4 minutes. ## Get started **1. Turn on developer mode on the TV.** Settings → Device Preferences → About → press **Build** 7 times. Then turn on **USB debugging** in **Developer options**. Stuck? Read the notes and warnings first. **2. Open Claude Code or Codex on your laptop.** The laptop and TV must be on the same Wi-Fi. **3. Paste this in.** ```text Help me clean up my Android TV and make it faster. My TV is a . 1. Before you change anything, tell me in plain words: this turns off system apps, and that has some risk. A few TVs got stuck at the logo or kept restarting, and you're an AI, so you can make mistakes. undo.sh and your undo list turn everything back on. Ask me to confirm I want to go ahead. 2. Connect to my TV over Wi-Fi. Walk me through anything I need to tap on the TV. 3. Before changing anything, list every app in plain English: safe to turn off, needed by the TV, and apps I use. Check free memory. 4. Ask me before every change. Turn apps off instead of deleting them. Keep a list of what you changed and how to undo it. 5. Never turn off: Google Play services (com.google.android.gms), Google Play, Settings, System UI, setup apps, the keyboard, Bluetooth, my HDMI inputs, the TV's input and tuner framework, or anything else the TV needs to start. On Google TV or Chromecast, also never turn off Google TV's home screen (com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx). If you're not sure, leave it on. 6. Install the home screen: download https://github.com/Ansub/tv-detox and run its install.sh with my TV and these apps: . 7. Turn off animations and make the TV sleep after 5 minutes. Then check the model name and ask me if the TV is OLED. Keep the screensaver on unless I say it's not OLED. 8. Wait 30 seconds after the last change, then restart the TV once and check it starts up normally before you say you're done. Show me free memory before and after. 9. Once everything is checked, remind me to turn off USB, Network and Wireless debugging (or Developer options) on the TV. Left on, other devices on my network can ask to control it. I only turn it back on for undo.sh or updates. ``` That's it. It asks you before every change. **4. Turn debugging off when it's done.** In **Developer options**, turn off **USB debugging**, plus **Network debugging** or **Wireless debugging** if you turned them on. Or turn off **Developer options** completely. ### Notes and warnings > [!WARNING] > **Do it at your own risk.** This turns off system apps. A few TVs got stuck at the logo or kept restarting, and the AI can make mistakes. It asks you before every change, and `undo.sh` plus its undo list turn everything back on. This is what worked for us, not professional advice. You're responsible for your own TV, and I'm not liable if something goes wrong. > [!WARNING] > **Google TV and Chromecast with Google TV:** don't turn off the TV's own home screen. On some of these devices that left them stuck restarting, and the only fix was a factory reset. Since v1.4.1, `install.sh` leaves it on for Google TV unless you opt in with `GOOGLE_TV=1`. The cleanup still works and makes the TV faster. You just keep Google TV's own home screen. > [!WARNING] > **OLED TVs:** keep the screensaver on. It stops a still picture from burning into the screen. Don't leave any home screen, this one included, on for hours. > [!NOTE] > **Turn debugging off afterwards.** While USB, Network or Wireless debugging is on, other devices on your network can ask to control the TV. Turn it off once setup is done, and back on only to run `undo.sh` or update. ## Help How do I turn on developer mode? 1. On the TV, open **Settings**, then **Device Preferences** (or **System**), then **About**. 2. Press OK on **Build** 7 times until you see "You are now a developer." 3. Go back, open **Developer options** and turn on **USB debugging**. If you see **Network debugging** or **Wireless debugging**, turn that on too. 4. The first time your laptop connects, the TV asks "Allow debugging?" Tick "Always allow" and press **Allow**. 5. When setup is done

quellen.name: MoneyPrinterTurbo README (features)
quellen.text: # MoneyPrinterTurbo 💸 ### An All-in-One AI Short Video Generator Provide a video topic or keyword, and MoneyPrinterTurbo will generate the script, match footage, create subtitles and background music, and produce an HD short video. ![Version](https://github.com/harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo/releases) ![Platform](https://github.com/harry0703/MoneyPrinterTurbo/releases/latest) ### Creation Workflows - [x] Use **AI Agent, WebUI, API, or CLI** workflows for quick creation or automated production - [x] Go from a topic to script, voiceover, footage, subtitles, music, and editing automatically, while retaining control over every stage - [x] Generate multiple output variants in batches, review task history, and import or export generation settings and API keys ### Scripts and Model Providers - [x] Use a ChatGPT subscription through OpenAI - Codex, with device-code sign-in and a dynamic model selector - [x] Explicitly choose ChatGPT Native OAuth for official app authorization and account-specific models; account/workspace eligibility and a local browser/runtime are required - [x] Generate or rewrite **multilingual video scripts** with AI, or supply a complete custom script - [x] Use leading providers including Kimi / Moonshot AI, OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Alibaba Cloud Qwen, Microsoft Azure OpenAI, ByteDance VolcEngine Ark, xAI Grok, MiniMax, and Xiaomi MiMo - [x] Connect through Shengsuan Cloud, APIMart, Cloudflare AI Gateway, Alibaba ModelScope, AIHubMix, AIML API, EvoLink, OpenRouter, API Route, Ollama, Claude Code subscription, OneAPI, LiteLLM, Groq, Pollinations AI, and other compatible gateways or local runtimes ### Video and Image Footage - [x] Upload your own **local images and videos**, or get HD stock footage from Pexels (free), Pixabay (free), and Coverr - [x] Generate `768P` or `2K` source footage with Metaso MiniMax H3, with 4–15 second clips in `9:16`, `16:9`, or `1:1` - [x] Create multiple AI video clips with Shengsuan Cloud AI Video, then combine them with the project's voiceover, subtitle, and editing workflow - [x] Use the native Volcano Engine Ark Seedance integration to generate cohesive visuals from individual script segments - [x] Turn script keywords into original video footage with WaveSpeed AI - [x] Access Seedance, Wan, and other text-to-video models through OFox with a single API key - [x] Generate 3–12 second AI video materials through the asynchronous MuAPI text-to-video API, with configurable endpoint, aspect ratio, resolution, and polling - [x] Connect OpenAI-compatible text-to-image services or custom image gateways and turn generated images into animated video clips - [x] Adjust clip duration, frame fitting, and material order to suit different aspect ratios and storytelling styles ### Voiceover, Subtitles, and Background Music - [x] Choose automatic voiceover, uploaded audio, or no voiceover, with voice samples and full narration previews - [x] Use **Edge TTS (free, no API key required)**, Azure Speech, SiliconFlow, Google Gemini, Xiaomi MiMo, MiniMax, ElevenLabs, Chatterbox, Kokoro, Fish Audio, ModelBest VoxCPM, and other voice services - [x] Generate subtitles and configure their font, position, color, size, outline, and background style - [x] Use random, local, or AI-generated background music with independent volume control ### Output and Publishing - [x] Export portrait `9:16 (1080×1920)`, landscape `16:9 (1920×1080)`, or square `1:1 (1080×1080)` videos - [x] Publish completed videos directly to **TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube Shorts** ## Gallery 🎬
